prompt: The query in the editor has one mistake. Fix it so that it answers this question: which campaign of each channel spent the most in 2025? Use the ad_spend_daily rows whose spend_date, a UTC day, falls in 2025; spend is in euros. Keep exactly one campaign per channel. When campaigns of a channel tie on spend, the lower campaign_id comes first. Return three columns, in this order: channel_name, campaign_id and spend, the campaign's 2025 spend. Return one row for each channel with spend in 2025. Any row order is fine.
hints: Next, check which ranking function the filter reads: the question wants exactly one campaign per channel.
A function that gives tied rows the same number keeps every tied campaign; one that numbers every row apart needs the stated tie-break as its last sort key.
starter_sql:
WITH campaign_spend AS (  -- one row per campaign with spend in 2025
  SELECT ch.channel_name, c.campaign_id, SUM(a.spend) AS spend
  FROM ad_spend_daily a
  JOIN campaigns c ON c.campaign_id = a.campaign_id
  JOIN channels ch ON ch.channel_id = c.channel_id
  WHERE a.spend_date >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND a.spend_date < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY ch.channel_name, c.campaign_id
),
ranked AS (  -- one row per campaign with spend in 2025
  SELECT channel_name, campaign_id, spend,
         RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY channel_name ORDER BY spend DESC) AS rn
  FROM campaign_spend
)
SELECT channel_name, campaign_id, spend
FROM ranked
WHERE rn = 1
why_this_works: ROW_NUMBER with campaign_id after the spend numbers tied campaigns apart, so rn = 1 keeps exactly one per channel.
